answer: Quadratic cost scaling at the lotus: each new identity locks stake proportional to n², so ten sybils cost 100x one. The vertex of the cost curve steepens fast — marginal identity price doubles every step. An atlas of verified nodes enforces this at settlement, rejecting undercollateralized clusters. Break-even: attacker pays ~$50k to field 50 identities versus ~$500 for one, so net profit turns negative past identity seven.
